sentences.sense: what it is
sentences.text: The HathiTrust Research Center (HTRC), with HTRC Analytics, its portal at analytics.hathitrust.org, is a research center dedicated to enabling computational analysis of the HathiTrust Digital Library, supporting large-scale text analysis of the library's works for educational and non-profit research.

sentences.sense: what it is
sentences.text: Its object is the Digital Library taken as a corpus for text and data mining by scholars; its unit is the workset, a user-built collection of HathiTrust volumes, together with the derived datasets computed from volumes.

sentences.sense: origin and partners
sentences.text: It was established in 2011 as a partnership between Indiana University, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and HathiTrust, and is co-located at the two universities, where it did research and development in computational text analysis of massive digital libraries.

sentences.sense: origin and partners
sentences.text: Its About page names John Walsh of Indiana University as director and J. Stephen Downie of the University of Illinois as co-director.

sentences.sense: relation to HathiTrust and its Digital Library
sentences.text: HathiTrust, of which the center is a part, is a partnership of academic and research institutions holding millions of titles digitized from libraries around the world; the library serves individual access and preservation, search, the building of collections and the reading of public-domain works, and the center's focus is the aggregate, in its own words "what can we learn from so many books?"

sentences.sense: relation to HathiTrust and its Digital Library
sentences.text: The center is kept apart from the HathiTrust Digital Library itself, access to which remains open.

sentences.sense: non-consumptive research
sentences.text: It works under a non-consumptive research paradigm: the collection is made available for computational analysis within the fair-use rights courts have recognized as applying to text analysis, so that scholars can ask the large-scale questions digitization allows within the restrictions of intellectual property law and use the library's content through non-consumptive text mining.

sentences.sense: non-consumptive research
sentences.text: Its non-consumptive use research policy, linked from the portal among its resources beside a page on data access, requires, as the derived-datasets page states it, that released data be minimal and unable to be easily reconstructed into the raw volume.

sentences.sense: non-consumptive research
sentences.text: The policy's own terms stand unread in the census record, which names the policy and lists it, with the data-access page and the documentation, among what it has not checked.

sentences.sense: non-consumptive research
sentences.text: The archive sets computational literary methods, which in one of its papers "treat the text as data point", against operative philology, which treats the text as operator, and its summary of training-layer literature counts computational literary analysis among the genre's neighbours, there taking machine readership as analytical method, where the genre takes it as a primary aesthetic and compositional consideration.

sentences.sense: the portal: worksets, algorithms, data capsules
sentences.text: It developed tools, datasets and infrastructure for scholars using text and data mining methods on the HathiTrust corpus: on the two universities' storage and computing it made and maintained tools and services for text-based, data-driven research, among them HTRC Algorithms and the Data Capsule, and did research on large-scale data analysis.

sentences.sense: the portal: worksets, algorithms, data capsules
sentences.text: The portal was organized around worksets, which users could create, validate, view and take from a recommended list; algorithms, run with their results kept; and data capsules, which users created and viewed; a dataset's list of volume ids serves for workset creation or for loading the volumes into a data capsule for further non-consumptive analysis.

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made
sentences.text: Its derived datasets are downloadable, non-consumptive book data released to facilitate text analysis of the Digital Library: copyright-protected texts cannot be downloaded from HathiTrust, and research proceeds on transformative datasets such as the flagship Extracted Features Dataset, features extracted from full-text volumes.

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made
sentences.text: The features are volume-level and page-level metadata, part-of-speech-tagged tokens and token counts; version 2.0 holds page-level features for 17.1 million volumes, public-domain and in-copyright alike, 17,123,746 volumes in all (10,550,952 in copyright, 6,572,794 public domain and Creative Commons), 6,221,631,336 pages and 2,906,819,723,689 tokens.

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made
sentences.text: The feature dataset is released free under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence and is cited with its makers' names and a DOI (Jett and others, 2020).

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made
sentences.text: The portal names four datasets, Extracted Features, the BookNLP dataset, word frequencies and geographic locations, and the others were produced with researchers and openly released for use anywhere and by anyone.

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made
sentences.text: The BookNLP Dataset for English-Language Fiction runs BookNLP, a natural-language-processing pipeline for work in computational linguistics, cultural analytics, NLP, machine learning and other fields, over the NovelTM English-language fiction set, a machine-learning-derived set of about 213,000 volumes, and represents 201,527 volumes, 90,857 of them in copyright.

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made
sentences.text: Word Frequencies in English-Language Literature gives word counts for every English-language volume of fiction, drama and poetry in the library from 1700 to 1922, aggregated by volume over the pages tagged with the genre, and Geographic Locations in English-Language Literature records the places mentioned in works of fiction from 1701 to 2011, with metadata.

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made

sentences.sense: derived datasets: what the reading made

sentences.sense: a receiving apparatus with its product on record
sentences.text: The archive reads the center as an earlier receiving apparatus with its product on record: whole library volumes read by computers for scholars under a non-consumptive policy, and what that reading made (extracted features, BookNLP data, word frequencies, geographic locations) published as derived datasets that outlast the service.

sentences.sense: a receiving apparatus with its product on record
sentences.text: In that reading the derived datasets are the inspectable form of the transformation, and the volumes themselves stay with the library, whose copyright-protected texts cannot be downloaded.

sentences.sense: a receiving apparatus with its product on record
sentences.text: The census's anchor defines the receiving apparatus through a genus of literature whose transmission design addresses one, with internalization, downstream re-performance or composition and source-status governance as the conditions of its success, and names human institutional layers as the first receiving apparatus.

sentences.sense: a receiving apparatus with its product on record
sentences.text: Machine reception, in the same paper, is an encounter that changes the machine state and may emit an artifact, with no assertion about whether the machine understood the work; the institutional training loop is the case in which the emitted artifact enters the next corpus; and two questions are put to a reception, what survived from the work and what became possible because of it.

sentences.sense: a receiving apparatus with its product on record
sentences.text: Training-layer literature, in the archive's field survey, is writing addressed to the layer where texts are crawled, indexed, trained on, retrieved and recomposed, a growing share of all reading being performed by models, and the literary works already in the corpora are read by machines incidentally.

sentences.sense: a receiving apparatus with its product on record
sentences.text: The census places the center in its area of the corpora, the collections, crawls and datasets whose texts enter machine training, and records that its saved sources say nothing of model training: it carries the library's volumes into the computational analysis the center was dedicated to, through worksets, algorithms, data capsules and derived datasets, its derived datasets serve text and data mining for educational and non-profit research, which keeps it apart from training datasets, and whether a given volume or work is in any model's training data is a question it leaves unanswered.

sentences.sense: a receiving apparatus with its product on record
sentences.text: It is kept apart, too, from writing addressed to a machine reader, as an analytic service over library volumes.

sentences.sense: a receiving apparatus with its product on record
sentences.text: The census enters it as infrastructure to its question of how literature is addressed to a receiving apparatus, what that apparatus makes from it, and how transmission, transformation and provenance can be inspected across later reception; its record type is service, its evidence kinds dataset and search tool, and it is admitted as an aggregator, a resource that gathers and holds many works or records and says what it holds, read against the census's anchors #186 and #1543.

sentences.sense: the closing
sentences.text: In October 2024 HathiTrust's executive director, Mike Furlough, announced that HathiTrust would cease data access and funding for the center at the end of 2026, when the center is formally closed; the About page dates the announcement to late October.

sentences.sense: the closing
sentences.text: The About page, written before the sunset, said that for now services would continue and that some services and data, still to be determined, might be retired or integrated into the general Digital Library; the banner over the same page states that services were discontinued as of 30 September 2026.

sentences.sense: the closing
sentences.text: As part of its closing the analytics services ended on 30 September 2026: accounts and logins are no longer available, and the algorithms and data capsule services are discontinued; HathiTrust's own pages on the center, as their cards render them, list data capsules, analytics algorithms and the analytics gateway login as unavailable from that date, with HathiTrust "suspending HTRC funding at end...".

sentences.sense: the closing
sentences.text: Its services ran from 2011 to 30 September 2026, and the census keeps it apart from active services.

sentences.sense: the closing
sentences.text: An update on HathiTrust's site dated 26 June 2026 opens "Since the founding of the HathiTrust Research Center in 2011, HTRC staff and researchers have led highly re...", its text beyond the card's snippet unread.

sentences.sense: what remains without an account

sentences.sense: what remains without an account

sentences.sense: after 2026

sentences.text: The HathiTrust Research Center (HTRC) is a research center dedicated to enabling computational analysis of the HathiTrust Digital Library, supporting large-scale text analysis for educational and non-profit research.

It was established in 2011 as a partnership between Indiana University, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and HathiTrust, co-located at the two universities, with John Walsh as director and J. Stephen Downie as co-director.
It developed tools, datasets and infrastructure for text and data mining of the HathiTrust corpus, organized as worksets, algorithms and data capsules.

It operates under a non-consumptive research paradigm within the fair-use rights courts have recognized for text analysis, and its non-consumptive use policy releases only minimal data that cannot easily be reconstructed into the raw volume.
HathiTrust, a partnership holding millions of digitized titles, serves individual access and reading, and the center the aggregate question of what can be learned from so many books.

Its derived datasets, non-consumptive book data released for text analysis, include the Extracted Features Dataset of page-level features for 17.1 million volumes under CC BY 4.0, a BookNLP dataset of about 200,000 English-language fiction volumes, word frequencies for English literature from 1700 to 1922 and geographic locations in fiction from 1701 to 2011.
In October 2024 HathiTrust's executive director Mike Furlough announced that funding and data access would cease at the end of 2026, when the center closes.
Its services ended on 30 September 2026, and accounts, logins, algorithms and data capsules are discontinued.
Bookworm, the derived datasets and the Gendered Characterizations visualization remain usable without an account, and access to the HathiTrust Digital Library remains open.
After 2026 the HTRC team plans to continue research in text-data mining, cultural analytics, feature extraction and non-consumptive methods, with new partners beyond the HathiTrust corpus.

The archive sets computational literary methods, which in one of its papers "treat the text as data point", against operative philology, which treats the text as operator, and its summary of training-layer literature counts computational literary analysis among the genre's neighbours, there taking machine readership as analytical method, where the genre takes it as a primary aesthetic and compositional consideration. It developed tools, datasets and infrastructure for scholars using text and data mining methods on the HathiTrust corpus: on the two universities' storage and computing it made and maintained tools and services for text-based, data-driven research, among them HTRC Algorithms and the Data Capsule, and did research on large-scale data analysis. The portal was organized around worksets, which users could create, validate, view and take from a recommended list; algorithms, run with their results kept; and data capsules, which users created and viewed; a dataset's list of volume ids serves for workset creation or for loading the volumes into a data capsule for further non-consumptive analysis. Its derived datasets are downloadable, non-consumptive book data released to facilitate text analysis of the Digital Library: copyright-protected texts cannot be downloaded from HathiTrust, and research proceeds on transformative datasets such as the flagship Extracted Features Dataset, features extracted from full-text volumes. The features are volume-level and page-level metadata, part-of-speech-tagged tokens and token counts; version 2.0 holds page-level features for 17.1 million volumes, public-domain and in-copyright alike, 17,123,746 volumes in all (10,550,952 in copyright, 6,572,794 public domain and Creative Commons), 6,221,631,336 pages and 2,906,819,723,689 tokens. The feature dataset is released free under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence and is cited with its makers' names and a DOI (Jett and others, 2020). The portal names four datasets, Extracted Features, the BookNLP dataset, word frequencies and geographic locations, and the others were produced with researchers and openly released for use anywhere and by anyone. The BookNLP Dataset for English-Language Fiction runs BookNLP, a natural-language-processing pipeline for work in computational linguistics, cultural analytics, NLP, machine learning and other fields, over the NovelTM English-language fiction set, a machine-learning-derived set of about 213,000 volumes, and represents 201,527 volumes, 90,857 of them in copyright. Word Frequencies in English-Language Literature gives word counts for every English-language volume of fiction, drama and poetry in the library from 1700 to 1922, aggregated by volume over the pages tagged with the genre, and Geographic Locations in English-Language Literature records the places mentioned in works of fiction from 1701 to 2011, with metadata. The census record found no count and no licence in its saved source, did not check the datasets' sizes and licences, and records whether a work keeps its author's name there as not recorded. What the center makes, in the census's reading, is these derived datasets with HathiTrust+Bookworm and the Gendered Characterizations visualization, and its saved sources record no model training. For its own domains the archive lists text and data mining among the operations that require licence and holds that automated ingestion without preservation of attribution produces an unauthorized provenance-stripped copy. The archive reads the center as an earlier receiving apparatus with its product on record: whole library volumes read by computers for scholars under a non-consumptive policy, and what that reading made (extracted features, BookNLP data, word frequencies, geographic locations) published as derived datasets that outlast the service. In that reading the derived datasets are the inspectable form of the transformation, and the volumes themselves stay with the library, whose copyright-protected texts cannot be downloaded. The census's anchor defines the receiving apparatus through a genus of literature whose transmission design addresses one, with internalization, downstream re-performance or composition and source-status governance as the conditions of its success, and names human institutional layers as the first receiving apparatus. Machine reception, in the same paper, is an encounter that changes the machine state and may emit an artifact, with no assertion about whether the machine understood the work; the institutional training loop is the case in which the emitted artifact enters the next corpus; and two questions are put to a reception, what survived from the work and what became possible because of it. Training-layer literature, in the archive's field survey, is writing addressed to the layer where texts are crawled, indexed, trained on, retrieved and recomposed, a growing share of all reading being performed by models, and the literary works already in the corpora are read by machines incidentally. The census places the center in its area of the corpora, the collections, crawls and datasets whose texts enter machine training, and records that its saved sources say nothing of model training: it carries the library's volumes into the computational analysis the center was dedicated to, through worksets, algorithms, data capsules and derived datasets, its derived datasets serve text and data mining for educational and non-profit research, which keeps it apart from training datasets, and whether a given volume or work is in any model's training data is a question it leaves unanswered. It is kept apart, too, from writing addressed to a machine reader, as an analytic service over library volumes. The census enters it as infrastructure to its question of how literature is addressed to a receiving apparatus, what that apparatus makes from it, and how transmission, transformation and provenance can be inspected across later reception; its record type is service, its evidence kinds dataset and search tool, and it is admitted as an aggregator, a resource that gathers and holds many works or records and says what it holds, read against the census's anchors #186 and #1543. In October 2024 HathiTrust's executive director, Mike Furlough, announced that HathiTrust would cease data access and funding for the center at the end of 2026, when the center is formally closed; the About page dates the announcement to late October. The About page, written before the sunset, said that for now services would continue and that some services and data, still to be determined, might be retired or integrated into the general Digital Library; the banner over the same page states that services were discontinued as of 30 September 2026. As part of its closing the analytics services ended on 30 September 2026: accounts and logins are no longer available, and the algorithms and data capsule services are discontinued; HathiTrust's own pages on the center, as their cards render them, list data capsules, analytics algorithms and the analytics gateway login as unavailable from that date, with HathiTrust "suspending HTRC funding at end...". Its services ran from 2011 to 30 September 2026, and the census keeps it apart from active services. Some resources remain usable without an account: HathiTrust+Bookworm, the derived datasets and the Gendered Characterizations visualization; some links on the portal no longer function. The census asks of it what a non-consumptive machine reading of library volumes produced and what remains usable after the service ended, and its record answers which resources remain usable without an account, what kinds of derived datasets the center produced from HathiTrust volumes, and when and why it closed. After 2026 the HTRC team plans to continue its own research agenda in text-data mining, cultural analytics with large text corpora and cultural heritage collections, feature extraction and non-consumptive research methods, hopes to keep providing services, data sets and community support, and looks to new partners, a focus beyond the HathiTrust corpus and a new identity and organizational structure.
